full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts for disposal of the appeal it brief, are that the appellants herein as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No. 64 of 2001 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Gobindagonj, Gaibandha, praying for declaration of their title in the suit land and confirmation of possession and also for a declaration that the SA Khatian No. 343 in respect of 78 decimals of land of plot No. 524 and 574 is incorrect. The plaintiffs' claim, inter alia, that one Newaz was the owner of 78 decimals of land of CS Khatian No. 339 and on his death the names of his heirs were recorded in the CS Khatian. At the time of SA survey the land of schedule Ka was recorded with the land of schedule Kia but the names of the predecessors of the plaintiffs were not recorded in the khatian by mistake. The plaintiffs were not aware of the wrong recording of khatian until the beginning of Poush 1407 BS. 

 8. Mr Zulhas Uddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that PW 1 Sattar Sheikh in his deposition specifically stated that as heirs and successors of Newaz, the original recorded tenants, they are in possession of the suit land measuring 78 decimals of land wherein the defendants have no right, title, interest and possession but the Court of appeal below without considering and discussing the deposition of PW 1 set-aside the judgement and decree of the trial Court and the High Court Division erroneously affirmed the judgement of the Court of appeal below. The learned Advocate further submits that the defendants contended in their written statement that the right, title and interest of Newaz in the suit land was sold in auction in Certificate Case No. 2845 of 1963 for arrears of rents and possession of the suit land was given to them, but DW 1 Md Liaquat All Sarker stated that he did not file any writ of delivery of possession in Court. So it is evidently proved that there was no auction of the suit property, but the High Court Division erroneously held otherwise. He also submits that PWs 2 and 3 corroborated PW I regarding continuous and uninterrupted possession of the suit land by the plaintiffs, but the Court of appeal below and the High Court Division without considering and discussing their evidence erroneously dismissed the suit. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the evidence of PWs have not been considered by the High Court Division while disbelieving findings of fact by lower Court and specifically the findings of fact of the trial Court that the defendants did not produce the sale certificate and the defendant did not assert that the sale certificate was registered and they did not make out any case that on what basis SA Khatian 343 was prepared, and that it is clear that the defendants hopelessly failed to prove that the suit land was sold in Certificate Case No. 2845/50-60, and moreover, the plaintiffs, as heirs of the original recorded tenant, are in possession of the suit property but the Appellate Court without setting aside those findings dismissed the suit and the High Court Division also without any findings of its own maintained the judgement of the Court below thus the decision merits interference by this Division. 

 13. The Court of Appeal below being the final Court of fact had also discussed the evidence of the respective parties in regard to the possession of the parties and came to a definite finding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession in the suit land. CS Khatian No. 339, Exhibit-I shows that the plaintiffs were the 'corfa tenants' under Rahim Uddin superior land lord, the predecessor of the defendants and Rahim Uddin eventually purchased the same through sale certificate, Exhibi t- 'Ga'.
